Behind every data point lies a child, a life, and a policy choice

Author

Vigneshwaran

Published

April 28, 2025

Behind every data point lies a child, a life, and a policy choice.

We begin our story with a world map of military spending, revealing how nations — including those with fragile economies — allocate significant resources to defense. This sets the stage for understanding how resource prioritization can shape social outcomes.

Turning to child health, we see that the same countries often lead in infant mortality, particularly for children between 1 and 59 months. These preventable deaths are not merely a public health failure, but a reflection of systemic underinvestment in healthcare and nutrition — often in favor of military or political agendas.

To explore the broader link between economic well-being and human outcomes, we zoom out with a scatterplot of GDP per capita vs. life expectancy. The trend is unmistakable: wealthier countries enjoy longer lives. But the scattered points tell another truth — not all countries convert wealth into well-being equally.

Finally, we focus on the life expectancy trajectories of the 10 hardest-hit countries. Some show modest gains, but all lag behind global progress. This emphasizes that historical disadvantage and underfunded health systems create long-lasting disparities, which aren’t easily reversed by short-term growth or aid.

In sum, these graphs collectively urge us to ask: how are national priorities shaping the lives — and deaths — of the most vulnerable?

!pip install geopandas

import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import requests, zipfile, io, os

# Download correct Natural Earth shapefile (Admin 0 - Countries, 110m resolution)
url = "https://www.naturalearthdata.com/http//www.naturalearthdata.com/download/110m/cultural/ne_110m_admin_0_countries.zip"

# Corrected download URL (the actual download site is hosted on Natural Earth mirrors)
correct_url = "https://www.naturalearthdata.com/media/natural-earth-vector/110m/cultural/ne_110m_admin_0_countries.zip"
response = requests.get(correct_url)
response.raise_for_status()

# Extract the zip file
z = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(response.content))
z.extractall("ne_110m_admin_0_countries")

# Read shapefile
world = gpd.read_file("ne_110m_admin_0_countries/ne_110m_admin_0_countries.shp")

# Load military data
metadata = pd.read_csv('unicef_metadata (4).csv')
military_df = metadata.dropna(subset=["Military expenditure (% of GDP)"])
latest_years = military_df.groupby("country")["year"].idxmax()
military_latest = military_df.loc[latest_years]

# Merge with world geometries
merged = world.merge(military_latest, left_on="ISO_A3", right_on="alpha_3_code")

# Plot map with annotations
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(18, 10))
merged.plot(column="Military expenditure (% of GDP)",
            cmap="Reds",
            linewidth=0.5,
            edgecolor="0.9",
            legend=True,
            legend_kwds={'label': "Military Expenditure (% of GDP)"},
            ax=ax,
            missing_kwds={"color": "lightgrey", "label": "No data"})

# Add text labels
for idx, row in merged.iterrows():
    point = row["geometry"].representative_point()
    value = row["Military expenditure (% of GDP)"]
    ax.text(point.x, point.y, f"{value:.1f}", fontsize=6, ha='center', color='black')

ax.set_title("Military Expenditure (% of GDP) by Country (Latest Year)", fontsize=16)
ax.axis('off')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

World Map of Military Spending

A choropleth map displays military spending by country, shading each nation according to the scale of its expenditure as a percentage of GDP. Darker shades indicate higher spending levels.

We observe that military spending varies greatly, with some lower-income countries investing disproportionately high percentages of their GDP, potentially diverting funds from essential social services.

!pip install geopandas

import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import requests, zipfile, io, os

# Set URL and headers (simulate a browser request)
url = "https://www.naturalearthdata.com/http//www.naturalearthdata.com/download/110m/cultural/ne_110m_admin_0_countries.zip"
fixed_url = "https://naturalearth.s3.amazonaws.com/110m_cultural/ne_110m_admin_0_countries.zip"
headers = {'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0'}

# Request with header to avoid 406 error
response = requests.get(fixed_url, headers=headers)
response.raise_for_status()

# Extract shapefile
z = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(response.content))
z.extractall("ne_110m_admin_0_countries")

# Load shapefile
world = gpd.read_file("ne_110m_admin_0_countries/ne_110m_admin_0_countries.shp")

# Load military data
metadata = pd.read_csv('unicef_metadata (4).csv')
military_df = metadata.dropna(subset=["Military expenditure (% of GDP)"])
latest_years = military_df.groupby("country")["year"].idxmax()
military_latest = military_df.loc[latest_years]

# Merge
merged = world.merge(military_latest, left_on="ISO_A3", right_on="alpha_3_code")

# Plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(18, 10))
merged.plot(column="Military expenditure (% of GDP)",
            cmap="Reds",
            linewidth=0.5,
            edgecolor="0.9",
            legend=True,
            legend_kwds={'label': "Military Expenditure (% of GDP)"},
            ax=ax,
            missing_kwds={"color": "lightgrey", "label": "No data"})

# Annotate with spending values
for idx, row in merged.iterrows():
    point = row["geometry"].representative_point()
    val = row["Military expenditure (% of GDP)"]
    ax.text(point.x, point.y, f"{val:.1f}", fontsize=6, ha='center', color='black')

ax.set_title("Military Expenditure (% of GDP) by Country (Latest Year)", fontsize=16)
ax.axis('off')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Bar Chart of Infant Mortality (1–59 Months)

A horizontal bar chart shows the 10 countries with the highest infant mortality rates for children aged 1 to 59 months. The countries are sorted in descending order by mortality rate.

Most of the top 10 countries are low-income or conflict-affected, suggesting a link between poverty, weak health systems, and child survival.

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the file (use your uploaded path in Colab)

plt.title("Top 10 Countries with Highest Infant Mortality Rate (1-59 months)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Scatter Plot: GDP per Capita vs. Life Expectancy

A scatterplot with a regression line plots GDP per capita (x-axis) against life expectancy (y-axis) for countries globally. Each point represents a country.

There is a clear positive correlation: countries with higher GDP per capita tend to have higher life expectancy. However, a few outliers indicate that income alone does not guarantee longevity — health investments matter.

Code 
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the metadata CSV
metadata = pd.read_csv("unicef_metadata (4).csv")

# Drop rows with missing values for relevant indicators
data = metadata.dropna(subset=["Life expectancy at birth, total (years)", "GDP per capita (constant 2015 US$)"])

# Create scatter plot with regression line
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.regplot(
    data=data,
    x="GDP per capita (constant 2015 US$)",
    y="Life expectancy at birth, total (years)",
    scatter_kws={'alpha': 0.4, 's': 15, 'edgecolor': 'black', 'linewidths': 0.2},
    line_kws={'color': 'red'}
)

plt.xlabel("GDP per Capita (constant 2015 US$)")
plt.ylabel("Life Expectancy at Birth (years)")
plt.title("Relationship between GDP per Capita and Life Expectancy")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Time Series Chart of Life Expectency

The Time series Chart shows how life expentency of country at birth has varied with the years for the ten most affected countries. While most countries show gradual improvement, their life expectancy remains consistently lower than the global average — highlighting persistent inequalities.

for country in top10_countries:
    country_data = life_expectancy[life_expectancy["country"] == country]
    plt.plot(
        country_data["year"],
        country_data["Life expectancy at birth, total (years)"],
        label=country
    )
